public_rationale: A dated evaluation records false factual assertions from an available LLM, checked against the subject's biography. That supports the ordinary claim that saying something does not establish its truth. Other models answered this particular prompt without detected errors; this does not make model assertions inherently authoritative.
limitations: The benchmark uses one person's biography and that person's manual judgments; it cannot establish a general error rate.
The cited report was published after the post but records tests within the target period.
This evidence does not settle consciousness, anxiety, or the accuracy of every model self-report.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: What LLMs say should not be taken as true just because they say it; treating their statements as truth misunderstands them.

statement.excerpt: It is a misapprehension of LLMs to confuse the things they say with what is true.

our_interpretation: The testable plain reading is that an LLM's assertion does not itself establish its truth. This does not mean all LLM statements are false.

Treat the claim as describing publicly available models in the current calendar quarter through publication, January 1–March 12, 2026. Technical evaluations have no fixed reporting cycle; this reporting window is an evaluator choice.
The assessment concerns factual reliability. It does not attempt to establish whether models have subjective experiences.
criteria.support_condition: Documented evaluations within the target period identify factual assertions by available LLMs that conflict with checked facts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes that factual assertions by the relevant LLMs reliably guarantee truth, and that the purported counterexamples are not genuine errors. Success on a limited test alone would not establish this.
